title: Design a measurable school pilot before asking institutions to commit
description: Audience: school and bootcamp decision-makers evaluating Zedu. Deliver a bounded pilot package: entry criteria, a 2-week evaluation plan, responsibilities, synthetic setup data, a scorecard and a go/extend/stop decision meeting. Measure agreed workflow completion, staff effort and unresolved blockers with explicit baselines; do not promise savings. Verify every proposed product step against the live app and mark missing access. Done when the team approves a reusable package with measurable success and exit criteria. Distinct from demo-request handling and general onboarding: this governs an institutional buying evaluation after a demo. No recruitment, account changes or pilot launch without approval.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Reuse the tech-club pilot rubric, fix its known gaps, and check every step in the app before anyone sees it
acceptedWorkstreams.description: This project already has a pilot agreement and rubric for a university tech club, and its review found three gaps worth fixing here: no weekly check-in, no stated source for each metric, and promises the team hadn't confirmed. Plan: 1) adapt that rubric for schools: entry criteria, a 2-week plan with a weekly check-in, named responsibilities, and a scorecard measuring workflow completion, staff effort and unresolved blockers, with the data source written next to each measure and a baseline taken in week 0; 2) build synthetic setup data and verify each pilot step against the live app (channels, Buzz, files, roles), marking any step that needs access we don't have; 3) write the go, extend or stop meeting agenda with explicit thresholds and no promised savings. Tasks: pilot package and scorecard (content), live-app step check (research).

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Write the pilot exit plan up front: what the school keeps, exports or deletes if it stops
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Schools hesitate to pilot when they don't know what happens to their staff's and learners' data afterwards. Approach: before the pilot starts, give a one-page exit plan covering what can be exported and how (verified against the current product), what is deleted and when, who confirms deletion, and how accounts are closed. Mark anything unverified for the team to confirm. Done: the exit plan template, the verification notes, and the line added to the pilot agreement. This lowers the cost of saying yes to a pilot.
